title: Perioperative glucose management protocol for insulin-treated patients having elective surgery
subtitle: Evaluation design to be settled against recruitment and theatre scheduling
statement: Insulin-treated patients having elective surgery at a teaching hospital receive inconsistent perioperative glucose management: variable insulin advice, infusions that run for days, and conflicting instructions. A local review found out-of-range capillary glucose on the day of surgery in 31 of 112 patients and postoperative values below 4 mmol/L in 9. A four-part protocol has been written; its effect on day-of-surgery glucose and its deliverability across general, orthopaedic and urological surgery are unknown.
whoAffected: About 150 insulin-treated adults a year having elective surgery, the pre-assessment and diabetes teams, theatre and ward staff.
whatHurts: Hyperglycaemia is associated with infection and hypoglycaemia while fasting is dangerous; conflicting instructions lead patients to change insulin on their own.
currentPractice: No written protocol; insulin advice varies by who sees the patient; infusions are started by default.
whyNow: A protocol is ready, a small departmental grant has been awarded, and the diabetes team is willing.
patientCenteredGoal: Patients receive one clear plan for their insulin, stay in a safe glucose range, and are not left fasting and uncertain.
summary: Problem framed around a four-part perioperative glucose protocol whose effect and deliverability are unknown.
